audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was given to Karma although whys[4] says the stage 'nets even: skill', and 2+ items was given to Illaoi although whys[6] ends 'it nets to skill'. Both layers agreed with each other but not with the text beneath them.
audit.why: The illaoi__karma mirror was already set with level 6, first item and 2+ items all Skill at 5/10 as one atomic group. Karma gains nothing at 6 because Mantra is live from level 1, and Inspire's move speed answers Leap of Faith's 450-range slam, so neither side owns the stage.
audit.corrected: Rows 4, 5 and 6 -> Skill in both layers as one atomic pair group, with the three phase whys and whys[5] rewritten so the reasons match the sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item stage claimed Illaoi's bruiser spike simply takes the window, with no counterplay and no numbers.
audit.why: Her item spike only converts if Test of Spirit lands, and that is a 16/15/14/13/12s ability at 900 range — inside Karma's 950 Q but slower than her poke cycle, so a sidestep is what decides the stage rather than the gold.
audit.corrected: whys[5] and phases[5].why now hang the stage on dodging a 16s, 900-range Test of Spirit instead of conceding it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Test of Spirit — named as the matchup-defining cooldown in five places — carries no cooldown and no range anywhere on the page, and Harsh Lesson's leap is never mentioned. 'Soulflare' is again used as the name of the Mantra-empowered Q.
audit.why: Test of Spirit is 16s at rank 1 from 900, which is what makes 'commit on its cooldown' actionable. Harsh Lesson is a 4s, 400-range leap that resets her attack and makes nearby tentacles swing, so it is the real burst tell in melee range. Riot names no Soulflare; the Mantra Q bonus is a delayed cataclysm.
audit.corrected: The 16s/900 numbers written into the do's and the cooldown block, the 4s Harsh Lesson leap added, and Soulflare replaced with Mantra-Q in whys[0], spikes[0] and wants.you[0].
